    - heading "Performance and limits" [level=1]
    - paragraph: Cortex separates user-visible response completion from asynchronous memory/graph completion and optional conversation-title work. This avoids coupling response latency to every indexing stage while retaining explicit consistency controls.
    - heading "Bounded workDirect link to Bounded work" [level=2]:
      - text: Bounded work
      - link "Direct link to Bounded work":
        - /url: "#bounded-work"
        - text: "#"
    - paragraph: Published policy bounds input/context/output tokens, tool steps, timeout, budgets and concurrency. Retrieval and transcript reads are paginated/bounded. Strict barriers capture finite cutoffs and configured deadlines; a hole or unavailable stage is an explicit result.
    - paragraph: Runtime client authentication defaults to 10,000 ms; RPC observation defaults to 12,000 ms, configurable within supported bounds. An issued mutation timeout reports uncertainty rather than cancellation/retry. Retain run/job identities for recovery.
    - paragraph: Private upload/delivery is capped at 20,000,000 decoded bytes; providers can impose smaller input limits. Reconnect snapshots retain bounded references rather than copying assets or upstream responses into browser persistence.
    - heading "Admission and answer completionDirect link to Admission and answer completion" [level=2]:
      - text: Admission and answer completion
      - link "Direct link to Admission and answer completion":
        - /url: "#admission-and-answer-completion"
        - text: "#"
    - paragraph:
      - link "submitAndStart":
        - /url: /api-reference/runtime-client#combined-admission-and-recovery
        - code: submitAndStart
      - text: combines admission and the start request in one parent mutation, bracketed by fresh session RPCs. This reduces the client admission path to three RPCs while retaining the original authority, approval, queue and identity checks. Authentication, observation and rendering are additional boundaries. Legacy manual APIs remain available, and a local timeout does not authorize a new intent or a blind execution retry.
    - paragraph: Display authorized response text as it arrives. Response completion is independent of later asynchronous facts/chunks/vectors and optional graph work; strict Agents still honor their captured memory barriers before execution. Optional title generation is scheduled after canonical answer finalization and can complete later. Do not include memory readiness or title completion in a first-visible-text measurement.
    - paragraph: Fresh Workflow starts initialize their original context-barrier steps inside the admission transaction using the official immediate-start contract. New V5 ordinary turns use one durable action for context preparation, the model step, canonical finalization and background-title enqueue. Strict stage waiting, server tools and explicit approval continuation remain Workflow-owned; historical journal versions are preserved. This removes the initial startup queue while moving guarded initialization work into admission, so measure both admission and first-visible-text latency. Agent streaming preserves whole received text fragments and publishes the first nonempty authorized fragment immediately. Later fragments retain bounded batching; every publication still checks current authority, transcript and source witnesses. These choices remove scheduling and word-delimiter buffering without promising an end-to-end latency bound.
    - paragraph: "Fresh Workflow executions first use bounded, authorized ingestion metadata to route potentially populated context to the existing retrieval action. This avoids repeating the full pending-context and profile probe before that action. Metadata alone never proves that context is empty: the empty path still runs the original pending-context, profile, source, authorization and fresh save checks in a separate mutation. A conservative metadata match can route to the action even when its full checks later find no indexed context. Existing V1–V4 journals retain their registered execution versions; new runs use V5. When the original empty-context proof completes, context saving, model-operation preparation and both policy-resolution checks share a native parent. Populated context uses the original retrieval body within the durable turn action, followed by fresh model preparation. Measure empty and populated memory separately on the installed cloud backend; source acceptance does not establish a latency improvement."
    - paragraph: Backend vector and fact retrieval overlap after the original read checks and validated query embedding. Successful results retain deterministic vector-first source bindings and context; failed reads do not publish or save context. Older adapters and tool wrappers retain their guarded serial path unless they explicitly support staged retrieval. This removes sequential retrieval work without adding a model call or retry.
    - paragraph: Private observation combines its initial session and authorized output read in one backend mutation, followed by a separate fresh session check before delivery. The canonical demo uses its existing final-authorization observer for run and memory status alongside the text transport, avoiding a separate duplicate status observer. Normal acquisition uses two RPCs; cursor resets and page draining can require further acquisitions. Current principal, scope, protected-source expiry and authentication generation still fence every delivered payload.
    - paragraph: Agent model preparation composes the original execution/operation handlers and both policy-resolution checks. Their results propose pinned model inputs; current authorization, qualification, source, transcript and budget controls still run at each billable admission/checkpoint. The outer pre-admission hydration, request binding, admission, parent binding and dispatch checkpoint share one transaction. These changes reduce database handoffs while retaining the current policy, source, lease and budget checks. Their installed latency must be measured separately from source acceptance.
    - paragraph: Selected native queries and mutations reuse raw principal, membership, grant, scope and tombstone records within one atomic invocation. Every authorization predicate still runs, returned records are detached, and database or child-mutation writes invalidate the retained reads. The next invocation reads current records again. Source retrieval, final memory delivery and private output observation retain their original read paths. This scope does not retain permissions, model decisions or authority across a network call or process lifetime.
    - paragraph: Empty-context preparation can also reuse raw deployment-policy and qualification rows within its own transaction. It fetches that metadata again before saving context, and every original policy, qualification and profile check still runs. This reuse does not cross transactions or replace source and delivery checks.
    - paragraph: Fresh installations store compact versioned references to the trusted compiled manifest. New accounts inherit the validated installed root. Existing full records remain supported without rewriting their data or financial history. The runtime still reads and validates current controls. Final memory delivery also shares profile and run-budget initialization for vectors with identical complete profiles and budget identities within one transaction; each vector retains its own authorization, source, chunk, receipt, hash and expiry checks. These changes require hosted measurements before reporting latency improvements.

    - paragraph:
      - text: The SDK's
      - link "RuntimeLatencyEvent":
        - /url: /api-reference/runtime-client#opt-in-client-latency-events
        - code: RuntimeLatencyEvent
      - text: includes version, phase, atMs and optional rpcId/method/durationMs. Pair events within the same client clock. Backend timestamps and browser/CLI clocks have different origins; do not subtract their absolute timestamps to invent an end-to-end duration. RPC settlement may occur after a local deadline, and a watcher wake does not imply that text was painted.
    - paragraph:
      - text: Workflow's deterministic handlers disable
      - code: process
      - text: ", so tracing safely defaults off inside those handlers. Use the actual Workflow journal's step start/completion metadata for memory barriers, context preparation, model steps and title enqueue. Native mutations also keep"
      - code: Date.now()
      - text: fixed within one transaction; a zero timestamp difference there does not prove zero execution time. Use native execution durations for those operations.
    - paragraph: Hosted Convex is the primary latency measurement environment. Run the canonical clients against a verified disposable cloud database and label the conditions. Docker can host those clients while the backend remains hosted; a local Convex benchmark is separate evidence.
    - paragraph:
      - text: The quickstart records first-text DOM commit from React's layout phase and schedules its after-paint marker with two animation frames, retaining document visibility metadata. The quickstart separately records
      - code: response.status.dom-commit
      - text: ","
      - code: transport.complete
      - text: and
      - code: answer.complete.dom-commit
      - text: ; canonical answer completion waits for the matching transported assistant message to be committed. Distinguish those markers from the first durable backend part and the first processed native stream text. The CLI's stdout acknowledgement is a separate boundary from a browser paint. Measure submission-to-visible text in the actual foreground application and report the selected boundary explicitly.
    - paragraph: The official Gateway provider internally acquires its service token and makes its HTTP request without exposing those subphase hooks. Native stream acquisition combines that opaque work. Processed-part/text markers are not raw network-first-byte measurements and do not reveal OpenAI internal queue timing.
    - paragraph: "A submission-to-first-visible-text duration below one second is a product target, not a measured result or service guarantee. The October 13 disposable hosted test of the unreleased 0.39 candidate measured the following actual canonical-client boundaries:"
    - table:
      - rowgroup:
        - row "Client and condition First turn Warm turn Below one second":
          - columnheader "Client and condition"
          - columnheader "First turn"
          - columnheader "Warm turn"
          - columnheader "Below one second"
      - rowgroup:
        - row "Vercel quickstart, foreground after paint 7.84 seconds 8.93 seconds No":
          - cell "Vercel quickstart, foreground after paint"
          - cell "7.84 seconds"
          - cell "8.93 seconds"
          - cell "No"
        - row "Basic CLI, first stdout acknowledgement 12.84 seconds 15.01 seconds No":
          - cell "Basic CLI, first stdout acknowledgement"
          - cell "12.84 seconds"

    - paragraph: Both clients returned their exact requested replies; native verification passed attributed facts, matching vectors, current authorization, complete usage and contiguous indexing through all eight events. The browser was signed out and closed before the CLI samples, and the disposable database and container were verified absent after testing. These are separate empty/populated-context conditions, not a controlled comparison with a historical release. The latency target remains unmet.
    - paragraph: The saved trace places model execution several seconds after run creation; retained model acquisition intervals are about half a second. Cortex orchestration, repeated validation and protected delivery dominate those samples. The published 0.35 and 0.37 legacy recall implementations have the same four awaited expressions, including parallel vector/fact reads; the newly measured backend runtime is an unreleased 0.39 path. This source comparison does not reconstruct a same-environment historical benchmark or assign an exact version-to-version slowdown.
    - heading "Measure the right statesDirect link to Measure the right states" [level=2]:

    - paragraph: Observe response, memory and graph latency separately. Use current profile metadata, contiguous watermark holes and durable job state to explain waiting. Configure graph only when needed and keep graph credentials in the worker service.
